Bindings per call, in test order:

| Call input | Bindings | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `{}` | 0 | Returns early at line 209 |
| `IsProd: None` | 2 | One free name gives 2 True/False combinations |

| `IsProd, IsDev, IsStage: None` | 8 | Three free names |
| `IsProd: {True}, IsDev: None` | 2 | `IsProd` is fixed in advance; only `IsDev` varies |
| `IsProd: {False}, IsDev: None` | 2 | Same, with `IsProd` fixed to False |
| `IsProd: {True}, IsDev: {False}` | 1 | Everything fixed, so one empty `{}` |
| `IsProd`, `IsDev`, `IsStage` all fixed | 1 | One empty `{}` |
| `IsStage, IsProd: None` | 4 | Keys stay in input order: `IsStage` first |
| `IsProd`, `IsStage` fixed; `IsDev: None` | 2 | Only `IsDev` varies |
| `GhostCondition: None` | 1 | Unknown name: the first binding happens, then a `KeyError` ends the generator |
| `Ghost1, Ghost2: None` | 1 | Same: only `{Ghost1: true, Ghost2: true}` |
| `Ghost, IsProd: None` | 1 | Same: only `{Ghost: true, IsProd: true}` |
| `IsProd: None` | 2 | Same as the second call |
| `IsProd: {True, False}` | 2 | `{True, False}` isn't fixed in advance, so `IsProd` varies |

Within each call the combinations run all-True first, then flip the last name first. For example: (True, True), (True, False), (False, True), (False, False).

This assumes the scenario cap `self._max_scenarios` is above 8, so it never stops a call early. I didn't check its value, but the total matches the observed count.
